claim: Transformative use examines whether the new work merely supersedes the objects of the original creation, or whether it adds new expression, meaning, or message.
evidence: The Court noted that a secondary work’s “new expression may be relevant” when assessing whether the use is of further purpose and different character, which is “a matter of degree,” but “it is not, without more, dispositive of the first factor.” If the addition of new expression, meaning, or message were determinative on the first factor, the Court cautioned that “‘transformative use’ would swallow the copyright owner’s exclusive right to prepare derivative works.”
